result.title: Give the Model a Finger: Developmentally Aligned Evaluation of Counting in Vision-Language Models
result.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) are exact on small sets and drift into estimation on larger ones, a profile reminiscent of children before they master counting. Children cross the barrier with epistemic actions: pointing at each item while reciting number words, moving counted items aside, partitioning the array. We give VLMs the same actions as dumb image tools with no visual intelligence of their own in a training-free agent loop. Our central claim is about measurement, not intervention: a model that counts by marking leaves a normally hidden serial procedure on the image, and the developmental principles of counting turn those marks into an interpretable audit of serial visual reasoning: every tag is classified against point-level ground truth as on-target, duplicate, phantom, or omitted, the answer is checked against the number of tags, and order irrelevance is tested by forcing opposite traversal orders. Across 9 models, 682 images, and 7 harness conditions we find that (i) the exact-counting range is a model-specific signature spanning nearly two orders of magnitude (R80 from 3 to 150 dots); (ii) as an intervention the finger mostly fails: tags help 4 of 9 models on small-count photographs, hurt imprecise pointers, and rarely beat a verbal routine or a blind point list; what the loop buys is an auditable trace, not accuracy; (iii) as measurement it succeeds: a tag-perturbation probe shows that precise pointers read their answers off the tags, pointing precision tracks which models benefit, dense scenes fail by omission, and models rarely revise after seeing their own tags; and (iv) the capacities dissociate: models follow an instructed traversal order yet often change their answer when it reverses, and children's regular-over-scattered advantage appears only under the routine and survives lattices that defeat a rows-times-columns shortcut.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在免训练的 agent loop 中，为 VLM 提供只能在图像上标记/指点的「手指」工具，借助发展心理学的计数原则审计其串行视觉推理；在 9 个模型、682 张图像、7 种条件设置下比较精确计数范围、干预效果与标签扰动等测量结果。
AI.relevance_reason: 其标签扰动探测与「遗漏」失败分析可直接核查 VLM 答案是否真正读取视觉证据、证据筛选是否完整，与 LVR 中答案使用、视觉旁路和动态获取证据的问题高度相关，但机制是外部显式标记而非内部 latent 状态。
